models.inverse_notes: Outer period solves as T2 = S*T1/(S-T1) and requires S > T1, which always holds when T2 > T1; check with Mars: 780×365.25/(780−365.25) = 686.96 ≈ 687 d. Inner period solves as T1 = S*T2/(S+T2); check with Mercury: 116×365.25/(116+365.25) = 88.04 ≈ 88 d. Equal sidereal periods (T1 = T2) admit no finite synodic period — the resonance singularity excluded by the guard. Do not publish rearrangements as separate records.
limitations: Excludes eccentric or inclined orbits whose angular speeds vary; the constant-ω derivation fails there.
Excludes the 1:1 resonance T1 = T2 (no finite synodic period); rejected by the ordering guard, not silently extrapolated.
Excludes N-body perturbations; ideal two-body relative motion only.
Source demonstrates Earth plus planet; the inner/outer generalization is an application profile justified by the body-agnostic relative-angular-speed derivation.

relationship.translation_notes: Solved either reciprocal form for the synodic period: with T1 the shorter (inner) and T2 the longer (outer) sidereal period, both orderings reduce to the single canonical expression S = T1·T2/(T2−T1), so no absolute value or branch is needed and the engine's lack of abs() is irrelevant. Generalizes Earth's P_0 role to any inner reference orbit about the same center (relative angular speed is body-agnostic). Dimensional check: count·count/count = count; inputs and output share one dimensionless day-count scale, so no conversion is inlined.
